title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Credit Policy — Number and Kind of Accounts a Business May Hold
content:
## Clauses

1. A business may hold at most **2** Ridgeline Pro Credit accounts at a time: at most **1** revolving account (Ridgeline Pro Revolving Charge or Pro Revolving Charge Plus) and at most **1** pay-in-full commercial account (any Ridgeline Commercial Account tier).
2. Ridgeline Pro Credit accounts are opened only for pro customer profiles; a consumer profile applies for Ridgeline Consumer Credit instead.
3. An account counts toward the limit while its status is applied, active or on hold.
4. A business may not apply for a revolving account while another revolving account in its name is applied, active or on hold, and may not apply for a commercial account while another commercial account in its name is applied, active or on hold.
5. No Ridgeline Pro Credit account in the business's name may be in charged-off status when a new application is submitted.

## Basis of each test

Each test is read from the company's records for the applying customer profile, as they stand before the application is submitted; it does not rest on what the caller says.

- **Profile type** (clause 2): the customer profile's type on record must be pro.
- **Same-kind account** (clauses 3 and 4): the accounts in that customer profile's name are matched by kind — revolving against revolving, commercial against commercial — and only those in applied, active or on-hold status count.
- **Charge-off** (clause 5): every Ridgeline Pro Credit account in the profile's name is looked at, of either kind; any one in charged-off status stands in the way.

## Status table for an existing account of the same kind

| Status of the existing same-kind account | Counts toward the limit | Blocks a new application of that kind |
|---|---|---|
| Applied | Yes | Yes |
| Active | Yes | Yes |
| On hold | Yes | Yes |
| Closed | No | No |
| Declined | No | No |
| Charged off | No | Clause 5 applies: no new application of either kind |

## Hypothetical cases

- A business holds an active Commercial Account Net 30 and applies for the Pro Revolving Charge: the existing account is of the other kind, so clause 4 does not stand in the way.
- A business holds a closed Pro Revolving Charge and applies for the Pro Revolving Charge Plus: a closed account does not count, so clause 4 does not stand in the way.
- A business holds an on-hold Pro Revolving Charge and applies for the Pro Revolving Charge Plus: both are revolving and the existing one is on hold, so the application may not be made.
- A business whose earlier Commercial Account Net 45 is charged off applies for a Pro Revolving Charge: clause 5 stands in the way although the kinds differ.
